A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tensor-Var research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Material moved or renumbered between versions can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original Lorenz-96, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, and ERA5 weather experiments, including satellite-track assimilation and ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain original experiments and add comparator results, anomaly-correlation evaluation, and a one-year rollout study.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 restricts the reconstruction-loss weight from [0,1] to (0,1], excluding a zero reconstruction term. This is a small refinement of the stated objective. The CME operators, history tensor product, architectures, and Algorithms 1–3 otherwise remain unchanged; an actual change in the training weight is not established.

E1.justification: The Lorenz-96, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, and ERA5 domains, atmospheric variables, and observation sources are retained. Appendix E.4.3 adds a one-year forecasting and assimilation stability scenario, extending temporal task requirements beyond v1's short-horizon evaluations without adding a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: V3 Table 2 adds '4D-Var by Adjoint' in all four chaotic-system settings, whereas v1 explicitly excluded adjoint models. V3 Figures 2 and 3 add FengWu 4D-Var (Xiao et al., 2024) to both weather comparisons, alongside the retained latent baselines. This substantially strengthens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V3 expands evaluation with optimization iteration counts, ACC as an additional weather metric, and a one-year forecast-only versus forecast-with-assimilation protocol. The rollout specifies six-hour steps, a five-step assimilation window, and seven-day forecast lead time. Adjoint-based evaluation is also introduced. Existing training budgets and dataset splits are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.4.3 and Figure 12 add a substantial long-term stability test against FengWu, separating autonomous forecasting from repeated assimilation. It exposes forecast divergence around step 800 that v1's short-horizon analyses did not reveal. The original history-length, feature-dimension, and Gaussian-kernel ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 evaluations with different initial conditions and 10 sampled sequences for satellite assimilation, reporting means and standard deviations. V3 extends the same reporting practice to additional results; no changed run counts, seed practices, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds adjoint and FengWu results, iteration counts, ACC curves, and year-long rollout findings. Existing values also change: Tensor-Var's KS-256 runtime rises from 17.37 to 21.37 in units of 10^-2 seconds. In Table 3, the ns=80, ds=120 ablation changes from 9.0 to 10.9 NRMSE%, while its Gaussian-kernel comparator changes from 14.3 to 11.7. Retained methods' main chaotic-system accuracy values are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B and Tables 1 and 4 introduce convergence-rate definitions and analyses of iteration counts and computational complexity for Tensor-Var, latent methods, conventional 4D-Var, and adjoint variants. These substantially extend the mathematical analysis. The original embedding and KKL convergence theorems are essentially retained, moving from Appendix A to Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces efficiency 'comparable to the static 3D-Var method' with a quantitative '10- to 20-fold speed improvement' claim. The central contributions—CME linearization, convex feature-space optimization, historical observations, learned features, and consistency guarantees—remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds an important applicability boundary: Appendix E.4.3 attributes long-rollout instability to limited expressiveness of linear dynamics and discusses an efficiency-versus-stability tradeoff against FengWu. Figure 12 locates divergence in forecast-only curves while assimilation remains controlled. Appendix B also explicitly acknowledges reconstruction error beyond feature-space optimization error. V1's state-access and covariance limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 supplies concrete settings for the added rollout, including the full 2018 evaluation period, six-hour steps, five-step assimilation window, and seven-day lead time. It also tightens the documented reconstruction-weight range. Existing architecture tables, optimizers, 200-epoch training, batch sizes, hardware, and data-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting kernel theory, optimization, adjoint methods, and recent dynamical forecasting, including Fukumizu et al. (2004), Givoli (2021), Cheng et al. (2025), and He et al. (2025). It removes v1's explicit delay-embedding discussion and associated Takens, Sauer, Krämer, and Uehara citations. The overall positioning against conventional and learned DA remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and preliminary explanations are revised, with copyediting throughout. A notation appendix and optimization appendix precede the retained theoretical and experimental material, and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. The main five-section narrative and most existing explanations preserve their original order and substance.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text. Figure 1 moves to the first page, and the original weather visualization moves to Appendix E.3. The ablation tables are merged and transposed; the benchmark table gains comparator rows and iteration counts. New theoretical tables, ACC plots, and rollout plots substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the empirical assessment through adjoint and FengWu comparisons and a long-rollout test that exposes a previously undocumented forecasting limitation. These additions strengthen comparison fairness and clarify applicability. However, the new abstract's 10–20-fold speedup claim is not representative of Table 2's roughly 1.1–2.7-fold advantages over adjoint 4D-Var, and implementation details for the new weather comparator remain limited. The evidence supports a qualified net improvement.
